text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) has elected its executive body, which gives equal representation to the trade unions and rightwing political parties. The board includes Janusz Tomaszewski, a regional Solidarity trade union leader, Marian Pilka, the leader of the Christian National Alliance, Kazimierz Kapera, who leads the Catholic families movement, and Adam Slomka of the Confedearation for the Independent Poland (KPN OP).
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's transport ministry and the European Commission will negotiate the liberalisation of the country's air transport market in September this year. Poland wants to liberalise the market gradually in several stages.

- A group of Taiwanese businessmen interested in imports of Polish agricultural products have visited the northeastern Olsztyn province to discuss their plans to create a food processing joint venture in the province, the Taipei Cultural and Economic Office in Warsaw said.

- The Atlantis construction material maker is planning to double its sales on the former Soviet Union markets, Atlantis president Pawel Obrebski said. In the next two years the firm will launch a new subsidiary in Russia's Kaliningrad special economic zone and a production plant in the Mielec special economic zone in southeastern Poland.

- Britain's Business Travel World has awarded the Polish flag carrier PLL LOT the Best East European Business Airline title for the second time. LOT's service quality placed it ahead of Lufthansa and British Airways.

- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecom monopolist, will activate 80,000 telephones by the end of 1997 in Warsaw, the company said. By 2000 the number of telephone subscribers in Warsaw will grow to 1.2 million.

- A dollar invested in Poland's economy results in a 40 percent growth of imports, the finance minister Marek Belka said. Current account deficit will not hurt the economy if it stays between 3 and 3.5 percent, Belka said.
NOWA EUROPA

- The general shareholders' meeting of the Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy has appointed a new supervisory board and decided to pay out 40 percent of the bank's net profit in dividend, the bank's president Cezary Stypulkowski said.
- Former PZU chairman Roman Fulneczek has been appointed president of the Petrus SA insurance firm co-owned by the state treasury, the Catholic Church and Italy's Fiat automaker.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The listed Mostostal Warszawa construction firm will construc an academic complex of the Warsaw Technical School's Material Enginnering department, worth 12 million zlotys, by the end of 1997, the companyu said.
ZYCIE
- Over 90 percent of Poland's washing powder market is controlled by international chemical concerns, a survey by the Chemical Industry Institute said.
